notes: Customer: QuickCortex builds bidding-time personalization for programmatic ads - decisions at <50ms are critical to bid competitiveness.
Primary ask: reduce per-decision compute cost while keeping P50/P95 latency tight. Interested in batching/caching tradeoffs but worried about added tail latency.
Engineering note: typical request = 60 token prompt + 25 token completion; heavy short-context workload during peak auctions (spikes 2-3x baseline for 300-600ms windows).
CTO comment: "We need to see perf numbers for 8-bit + layernorm-safe quantization. If quality holds, dedicated pool economics look promising."
SE notes: early test showed ~30% cost savings using KV-prefix caching for repeated user history; however p95 increased by ~12ms under default batching settings.
Business: procurement wants predictable monthly committed spend; will consider Redwood Dedicated with burst capacity if SLA/latency hold.
Quote request: include A/B fallback plan to hosted API if private capacity hits limits (auto-route by latency SLO).
Ask to RDW team: provide microbenchmark harness (we sent QC token distribution + sample prompts) and run: 1) baseline hosted v2, 2) quantized 8-bit, 3) batching @ 8/16/32, 4) prefix caching enabled.
perf_targets: Throughput target: sustained 2k requests/sec with <10% tail amplification
Cost target: <$0.003 per decision (incl. overhead) or <$0.20 per 1k decisions)
Quality gates: BLEU/ROUGE delta < 1.5% vs float32 baseline; manual eval on 200 golden queries
poc_plan: Week 1 - baseline perf run (no quant, no cache) on candidate model set; capture token-level breakdown
Week 2 - enable KV-prefix caching (hot-user flows); measure hit-rate and end-to-end latency impact
Week 3 - run quantization profiles (8-bit per-tensor, QAT not requested yet); validate quality vs baseline
Week 4 - stress test batching configs (8/16/32) under synthetic peak; measure p95 amplification and cost/k-token
Deliverable - consolidated benchmark deck + recommended Dedicated pool size and quantization profile; ops runbook for routing fallbacks
final_notes: Customer pragmatic: wants measurable unit-economics improvements before committing. Strong chance to upsell Optimize + Dedicated if benchmark meets targets. Security sign-off (KMS + SOC2) is gating for Private deployment.
